title: Lenskart investors sell over $1 Bn stake in 3 months; SoftBank offloads another $300 Mn
summary:
SoftBank has sold another 4.5 crore shares of eyewear retailer Lenskart for around Rs 2,888 crore (over $300 million) through a block deal, making its second large sell-off in the company since June.
According to the stock exchange, the shares were sold at Rs 641.75 each, taking the total value of the transaction to Rs 2,888 crore. SoftBank held 17.14 crore Lenskart shares, or a 9.69% stake, as of July. Following the latest sale, its holding has fallen to around 12.64 crore shares, or about 7.15%.
The latest transaction comes less than three months after SoftBank sold Lenskart shares worth around Rs 2,873 crore in June. It had sold around 5.65 crore shares at Rs 508.55 each in that transaction.
SoftBank is not the only early investor to have reduced its stake in Lenskart in recent months. Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA) sold shares worth around Rs 1,960 crore in June, while Temasek offloaded shares worth around Rs 1,940 crore in July.
Together, these four transactions, including SoftBank's two sales, amount to around Rs 9,660 crore (over $1 billion) worth of Lenskart shares sold by large institutional investors since June.
The sell-offs come as Lenskart continues to see strong investor interest in the listed eyewear company. The company made its stock market debut in November 2025 and has since seen several large institutional transactions.
The latest block deal saw shares picked up by a mix of institutional investors, including Societe Generale, Motilal Oswal Mutual Fund, SBI Mutual Fund, Sundaram Mutual Fund and global funds.
During its latest quarterly results (Q1 FY27), the company posted 43% year-on-year growth in its revenue to Rs 2,714 crore with a profit of Rs 228 crore. The company closed its trading session at  Rs 658.75, with a total market capitalization of Rs 1,14,225 crore.

title: Y Combinator sells Rs 970 Cr Meesho stake in block deal
summary:
Global startup accelerator Y Combinator has sold shares worth around Rs 970 crore in Meesho through a block deal on the stock exchanges, marking another major exit by an early investor in the ecommerce company.
According to data available on the NSE, Y Combinator sold around 4.84 crore shares worth Rs 969.63 crore in the transaction. The deal comes weeks after other early backers of Meesho, including Peak XV Partners and Elevation Capital, offloaded Rs 1,949 crore worth of holdings in the company.
The latest transaction is part of a broader trend of early Meesho investors monetising their investments after the company went public. Meesho listed on the stock exchanges in December 2025 following its IPO.
Prior to the transaction, Y Combinator was expected to sell up to a 1.05% stake in Meesho for around Rs 957.5 crore, with the proposed sale price set at Rs 197.5 per share. However, the executed transaction on the NSE was valued at Rs 969.63 crore.
Earlier this month, Peak XV Partners and Elevation Capital sold around 10.48 crore Meesho shares in a block deal worth nearly Rs 1,949 crore. Both investors sold around 5.24 crore shares each at Rs 186 apiece.
Meesho, founded by Vidit Aatrey and Sanjeev Barnwal, operates an ecommerce marketplace focused on value-conscious consumers and sellers across India.
The latest exits also highlight the significant liquidity available to Meesho’s early investors after its public listing. While these transactions allow investors to book returns, continued selling by large shareholders can also keep the stock under pressure.
During the previous quarter (Q1 FY27), the company posted a 48% year-on-year increase in operating revenue to Rs 3,713 crore, while its net loss narrowed 54% to Rs 133 crore from Rs 289 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal.

title: Healthify merges with US-based Berry Street
summary:
Bengaluru-based healthtech startup Healthify has merged with US-based nutrition care company Berry Street in an all-stock deal. 
The merger will combine Healthify’s AI-led health platform with Berry Street’s insurance-backed clinical care network in the US. 
The combined company will operate under the Healthify brand in India and other international markets, while continuing with the Berry Street brand in the US. Healthify founder and CEO Tushar Vashisht and Berry Street founder and CEO Noah Kotlove will serve as co-CEOs.
Healthify’s AI platform, including its nutrition assistant Ria, will be integrated with Berry Street’s network of more than 2,000 clinicians operating across all 50 US states. 
Berry Street provides virtual nutrition care through registered dietitians and handles insurance, billing and administrative services. 
The merger is aimed at building an insurance-covered AI-powered metabolic health platform in the US, with a focus on conditions such as obesity and diabetes.
 Healthify had been expanding in the US and identified insurance coverage as a key requirement for scaling its nutrition and health services there. 
Founded in 2012, Healthify has raised around $150 million from investors including Khosla Ventures, Blume Ventures and Chiratae Ventures. The company said the combined business will continue expanding its AI capabilities and explore new international markets.

title: Morgan Stanley-backed Sterling Accuris reports Rs 231 Cr revenue in FY26; losses widen 38%
summary:
Diagnostic and pathology services chain Sterling Accuris’ revenue growth slowed to 16% year-on-year during the fiscal year ending March 2026, compared with in FY25. Meanwhile, the Ahmedabad-based firm also saw its losses widened by 38% during the year.
Sterling Accuris’ revenue from operations grew to Rs 230.7 crore in FY26 from Rs 198.3 crore in FY25, its consolidated financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC) show.

Founded in 2014, Sterling Accuris Diagnostics provides a range of diagnostic and pathology testing services across India. The company offers more than 2,000 tests through a network of over 250 laboratories and collection centres spanning 50+ cities. It claims to have conducted more than 10 million tests to date. Testing services remain the company’s sole source of revenue.
The firm earned an additional Rs 2.9 crore from non-operating sources, taking its total income to Rs 233.6 crore in FY26 from Rs 201.8 crore in FY25.
For the diagnostics firm,  employee benefits remained its largest expense at Rs 59 crore, rising 14% year-on-year. Materials used for testing and diagnostics increased 16% to Rs 52.2 crore, while fees paid to doctors and pathologists stood at Rs 42.8 crore.
Depreciation and amortisation expenses stood at Rs 20.66 crore, while advertising and promotional expenses surged 84% to Rs 10.5 crore. Overall, the company’s total expenses increased 17.5% to Rs 259.5 crore in FY26 from Rs 220.9 crore in FY25.
With expenses growing faster than revenue, Sterling Accuris Diagnostics’ profitability weakened in FY26. The company’s net loss widened 38% to Rs 32 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 23.2 crore in FY25.
However, the firm remained EBITDA positive at Rs 2.8 crore during FY26, with an EBITDA margin of 1.2%. Its ROCE stood at -7.9% during the year.

On a unit basis, Sterling Accuris spent Rs 1.12 to earn a rupee of operating revenue in FY26. As of March 2026, the company had current assets worth Rs 57 crore, including Rs 23 crore held in cash and bank balances.
Sterling Accuris competes with players such as Y Combinator-backed Orange Health, which clocked Rs 139 crore in revenue in FY26. PharmEasy-owned Thyrocare reported Rs 829 crore in revenue and Rs 163 crore in profit during the same fiscal year. Redcliffe Labs posted Rs 419 crore in revenue in FY25, while Healthians reported Rs 263 crore and narrowed its loss to Rs 5 crore. The FY26 financials of Redcliffe Labs and Healthians are yet to be filed.
Sterling Accuris has raised a total of $33 million in funding to date. Its lead investors are Morgan Stanley, holding a 35.64% stake, and Udhay Vi Realty, with a 17%.

Digital and AI-native bank slice has appointed Samir Sawhney as Executive Director and Ramesh Kumar as Independent Director to its board. Both appointments have been approved by the slice board, while the Reserve Bank of India has also approved Sawhney’s appointment as Executive Director.
Sawhney brings over three decades of banking experience across treasury, investment management and retail banking. Until recently, he served as chief executive of RMBS Development Company, set up by the National Housing Bank to develop India’s residential mortgage-backed securities market.
Before this, Sawhney spent over 34 years at State Bank of India, where he served as Chief General Manager, Global Markets, and headed the bank’s treasury operations. He also served as chairman of FEDAI.
Kumar brings more than 30 years of experience across banking, financial services and technology. He spent two decades at ICICI Bank, where he led technology strategy and digital banking platforms. Earlier, he led core banking implementation at State Bank of India.
Kumar had also worked with slice as an advisor during its integration and merger with North East Small Finance Bank. His areas of expertise include technology governance, cybersecurity, operational resilience and digital transformation.
Slice said it will focus on growth and responsible underwriting while continuing to invest in technology.
Following its merger with North East Small Finance Bank, slice operates as a full-stack bank offering savings accounts, fixed deposits, UPI, borrow, credit cards and an UPI-led bank branch.
Slice is backed by investors including Tiger Global, Insight Partners, Advent International, Blume Ventures and Gunosy Capital.

title: Endiya Partners leads $2.5 Mn seed round in physical AI startup WATER
summary:
Physical AI company WATER has raised $2.5 million in a seed funding round led by early-stage venture capital firm Endiya Partners, with participation from Pullela Gopichand, Rohit Chennamaneni, Nandan Reddy, and other angel investors.
The fresh funds will be used for technical validation as the company works to develop an intelligence layer for adaptive surfaces, with potential applications across automotive, aviation, and other sectors, WATER said in a press release.
Founded in 2024 by Teja Vinukollu and Haneesh Mourya Desu, WATER develops adaptive surfaces, including the FLOW chair and CAMA bed, powered by VORTEX, its foundational model for understanding how the human body interacts with the physical environment.
The Hyderabad-based startup said its products use a combination of sensing, decision-making, and physical actuation to respond to the human body in real time. FLOW focuses on posture, movement, and load during seated interaction, while CAMA focuses on sleep, recovery, and respiration.
WATER said it plans to extend the underlying technology beyond chairs and beds to other physical environments, where surfaces and systems can adapt to individual needs.
The adaptive intelligent surfaces segment is still at an early stage in India, while the broader Physical AI and deeptech ecosystem is seeing growing investor interest.
Recently, Invisel raised Rs 4 crore in a funding round led by IAN Angel Fund, while Bengaluru-based Mowito secured $3 million in pre-seed funding to develop Physical AI foundation models for industrial robots. Flo Mobility also raised $2.5 million in a pre-Series A round to scale its Physical AI-powered autonomous solutions for construction. title: Third Wave Coffee raises Rs 408 Cr led by WestBridge
summary:
Bengaluru-based coffee chain Third Wave Coffee has raised Rs 408 crore (43 million) in a funding round led by existing investor WestBridge Capital, with most of the capital coming through a primary issuance. The round also saw participation from existing investor Creaegis and other angel investors. 
The new funding will support expansion in existing markets, increase presence in high-potential cities and accelerate its Third Rush Desserts segment, the company said in a press release.
According to a Mint report, the latest round values Third Wave Coffee at around Rs 2,000 crore ($210 million), compared to Rs 1,200 crore (150 million) during the previous funding round.
The company plans to enter nine new cities in the coming months, including Ludhiana, Jalandhar, Amritsar and Lucknow. It also plans to deepen its presence in tier II and tier III cities.
Third Wave Coffee, founded in 2017 by Sushant Goel, Ayush Bathwal and Anirudh Sharma, operates cafes and sells products such as coffee beans and cold brew bags. The company is present across Bengaluru, Delhi, Pune, Mumbai and Hyderabad, among other cities.
WestBridge has been an investor in Third Wave Coffee since its Series A round. It led the company’s $21 million Series B round in 2022, while Creaegis led its $35 million Series C round in 2023.
The latest round takes Third Wave Coffee’s total funding to more than $105 million.
Soon after the 2023 fundraise, Third Wave Coffee laid off around 100 employees. Around the same period, co-founder and then CEO Sushant Goel stepped down from the CEO role and moved to the company’s board. Rajat Luthra, former CEO of KFC India and Nepal, was appointed as his replacement.
In FY25, Third Wave Coffee’s operating revenue stood at Rs 285 crore, while its net loss narrowed to Rs 94 crore. The company has yet to file its FY26 financials.

The Bengaluru-based startup had previously raised Rs 28 crore in a pre-Series A round led by RPSG Capital, with participation from existing investors OTP Ventures and Huddle Ventures, as well as angel investors Suyash Saraf and Anisha Agarwal Saraf, in September last year.
The proceeds will be used for research and development, product expansion, distribution and hiring, Asaya said in a press release.
Founded in 2021 by Neeraj Biyani, Eeti Sharma and Mandeep Singh Bhatia, Asaya offers skincare products targeting hyperpigmentation, dehydration and acne. Its portfolio includes dark spot correcting serums, even tone creams, body sprays, cleansers and sunscreens.
The brand follows a D2C model and sells through its own online channels, quick-commerce platforms and select offline retail outlets.
Asaya has developed a proprietary molecule called MelaMe, which it says is designed to address pigmentation and uneven skin tone, particularly for Indian skin types.
The Indian D2C skincare segment has seen growing investor interest, with brands focusing on science-backed, ingredient-led and premium skincare products.
RAS Luxury Skincare secured a Rs 60 crore investment from Dabur in March 2026, while Chosen raised $5 million in a Series A round led by Fireside Ventures in May. KorinMi raised Rs 10 crore from Lotus Herbals' innovation fund in June, while functional skincare startup Clarity Labs secured over Rs 4 crore in seed funding.
Earlier funding activity has also included skincare and personal-care brands such as Innovist, which owns Chemist at Play, and Pilgrim.

title: D2C Insider concludes AI summit Frontier to explore AI’s role in consumer businesses
summary:
D2C Insider concluded Frontier, a D2C AI Summit, in Gurugram, bringing together more than 150 D2C founders and CXOs, over 25 AI leaders and representatives from more than 100 brands to discuss how artificial intelligence is reshaping consumer businesses.
The event focused on the impact of AI across discovery, customer conversations, conversion, retention, operations and unit economics, rather than treating AI as a standalone technology.
The agenda examined how AI could influence consumer brands’ business models and P&Ls as companies move from experimenting with individual AI tools to integrating the technology across their operations.
The summit featured four AI bootcamps, four operator-led panel discussions, a fireside chat, networking sessions and an AI Experience Zone.
The event opened with a workshop by Pradeep Sekhar, India CEO of Base.com, on deploying AI agents to monitor real-time omnichannel profitability.
This was followed by a panel discussion titled “The AI-Native Consumer: How AI Is Rewriting Discovery, Conversation & Conversion”. The panel featured Ojasvi Bhatia, Lead AI Partnerships, India at Meta; Apurva Mudgal from Product at WhatsApp; Ayushi Gudwani; Vaibhav Makhija; Aditya Singhal; and Sahil Jindal, Managing Director of the Jindal Group.
The pre-lunch session focused on the technology infrastructure supporting AI adoption. The afternoon opened with a fireside chat hosted by Abhishek Shah, featuring Gaurav Mangla, CEO of fastrr by Shiprocket, and Nitin Agarwal. This was followed by a workshop on autonomous AI.
Commenting on the objective behind the summit, Abhishek Shah, Chief Evangelist at D2C Insider, said that while many founders have experimented with AI tools, relatively few have integrated AI into their core business operations.
The summit also featured an AI Experience Zone, speed networking sessions and curated founder introductions based on participants’ business stage, category and growth ambitions.
Drawing from D2C Insider’s community of more than 30,000 D2C founders and operators, Frontier provided a platform for entrepreneurs and ecosystem players to discuss AI adoption and explore potential collaborations.

title: A91 invests Rs 143 Cr in Atomberg, sells Rs 445 Cr stake while retaining 21%
summary:
A91 Partners has invested around Rs 143 crore in consumer appliances startup Atomberg through primary and secondary transactions, and has already sold shares worth around Rs 445 crore, according to the company’s draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) filed ahead of its proposed initial public offering (IPO).
The disclosures show that A91 invested around Rs 118 crore as primary capital in Atomberg, while another Rs 25 crore was invested through secondary transactions. The secondary purchases helped provide an exit to some of the company’s early shareholders, including founders and Parampara Early Stage Opportunities Fund.
The investment has generated a significant return for A91. Against its total investment of around Rs 143 crore, the fund has sold shares worth approximately Rs 445 crore. Despite these partial exits, A91 continues to remain Atomberg’s largest shareholder with a 21.02% stake as of the DRHP date.
A91’s investment in Atomberg dates back to 2019, when it led the company’s Series A round. The investor also participated in Atomberg’s Series B round in 2020.
The latest DRHP disclosures also highlight the broader secondary transactions that have taken place at Atomberg over the years. Early investors, founders and other shareholders have sold shares worth around Rs 683 crore since 2019. A91 was the largest seller, with sales worth about Rs 445 crore, followed by Parampara, which sold shares worth around Rs 116 crore. Atomberg’s co-founders Manoj Meena and Sibabrata Das also sold part of their holdings.
Founded by Meena and Das, Atomberg started with energy-efficient BLDC fans and has expanded into other home and kitchen appliances. The company reported Rs 1,293.77 crore revenue from operations in FY26, up 34.8% year-on-year, while its net loss stood at Rs 149 crore.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [Aug 17 - Aug 22]
summary:
This week, 21 Indian startups raised $198.33 million across 3 growth-stage deals, 14 early-stage deals and 4 undisclosed rounds. The week also saw 8 key hires, 2 departures and 2 mergers and acquisitions.

In contrast, 14 startups had collectively secured about $151.5 million in the previous week.
[Growth-stage deals]
Growth-stage startups raised $118.3 million across three deals this week. Fintech unicorn Navi led the segment with a $100 million investment from Prosus in its first institutional funding round. Electric two-wheeler maker BGauss raised Rs 110 crore ($11.6 million) in a Series D round, while Mumbai-based paediatric behavioural health platform Butterfly Learnings secured Rs 65 crore ($6.7 million) in a Pre-Series B round led by Inflexor Ventures.
[Early-stage deals]
Early-stage startups raised $80.03 million across 14 deals this week. CtrlS led the segment with Rs 250 crore, including Rs 200 crore from Zerodha cofounder Nikhil Kamath and Rs 50 crore from entrepreneur Sreeram Reddy Vanga. NeoGeo raised $20 million in a Series A led by Neev II Fund and Aavishkaar Capital, while Rezolv secured $12.5 million in a Series A led by Norwest.
Peeko raised over $7 million in a Series A led by Chiratae Venture, while healthtech platform Lissun raised Rs 48 crore in a Series A led by Colossa Ventures.
Other startups that secured funding this week included DeHaat Honest Farms, a pesticide-free food brand by DeHaat, deeptech startup AlgoFET, specialty coffee brand First Coffee, reusable packaging platform Yantra Packs and five other early-stage ventures.
Events and ticketing platform BookMyShow, traveltech startup Atravelq, healthtech infrastructure startup Tross and water infrastructure startup Neuromod Aqua also raised funding this week, although the amounts remained undisclosed.
[City and segment-wise deals]
Bengaluru continued to lead the funding charts with 9 startup deals during the week, followed by Delhi-NCR with 7 deals. Mumbai, Hyderabad and Jaipur also recorded  deals this week.

Segment-wise, e-commerce startups led the week with five deals, followed by healthtech with three. Fintech and deeptech startups secured two deals each, while data centres, AI, EV, agritech, F&B and other sectors also recorded deals.
[Series-wise deals]
Series A and Seed rounds led the week with five deals each, followed by pre-Series A and pre-Series A rounds with three deals each. Pre-IPO, Series D and pre-Series B and others also recorded one deal each during the week.

[Week-on-week funding trend]
On a weekly basis, startup funding increased 31% to $198.33 million from $151.5 million raised in the previous week.
The average weekly funding over the past eight weeks stood at around $297 million across 20 deals.
[Key Hirings / Departures]
This week, Bengaluru-based quick home services platform Snabbit appointed Pradeep Yadav as Head of Operations, while healthtech startup Superhealth named former Dunzo cofounder Dalvir Singh Suri to the same role.
Swiggy expanded the roles of three senior executives across Instamart and its Food Marketplace, appointing Himavant Kurnala as Chief Growth and Product Officer, Nitesh Garg as CTO and Saurav Goyal as COO of the Food Marketplace. MobiKwik also appointed former Bajaj Markets executive Manish Pathania as CBO.
Charwaha.com appointed Bhanu Dasgupta as Co-Founder and Chief Strategy and Sales Officer, while wealth and asset management firm 360 ONE named Abhishek Bhalotia as Chief Growth & People Officer.
Departures: Walmart-backed ecommerce major Flipkart is set to see two senior leadership exits, with Gunjan Bhartia, Senior VP of Business Finance, and Amer Hussain, VP of Supply Chain for Grocery and Minutes, stepping down from their roles.
[Mergers and Acquisitions]
DSP Finance, the NBFC arm of DSP Group, acquired Salter Technologies, which operates digital lending platform Volt Money and offers loans against financial assets, including mutual funds.
AI-native fleet and logistics technology company Fleetx.ai acquired transportation management system provider Pando.ai for an undisclosed amount.
Hearzap completed its acquisition of Amplifon India’s hearing healthcare business, following the definitive agreement announced in May 2026.

The launch marks the next phase in 1% Club’s evolution from a financial education platform into a technology-led personal finance ecosystem, with the AI CFO helping users understand their finances, evaluate decisions and access tailored guidance across their financial journey.
Swiggy has launched ‘Guru’, a 24x7 AI business assistant built for India’s restaurant industry to help partners make data-driven decisions, track performance and manage day-to-day operations through a conversational interface. Available across 720+ cities and 2.7 lakh+ restaurants, Guru supports sales analysis, payouts, ad campaigns, discounts and menu insights in 20+ vernacular languages.

title: Exclusive: Battery Smart raises $19.5 Mn at $430 Mn valuation
summary:
EV battery-swapping startup Battery Smart has raised Rs 185.5 crore or $19.50 million in its Series C funding round led by existing investors Rising Tide Ventures with the participation from Ecosystem Integrity Fund and Blume Ventures.

In March 2026, the company had raised Rs 66 crore in a pre-Series C round from Acacia Inclusion, Blume Ventures and PC-SBI Kurashi Visionary Fund, a funding round reported exclusively by Entrackr. This was followed by a $15 million debt funding from Mirova in April.
The board at Battery smart approved the allotment of 34,094 Series C CCPS at an issue price of Rs 54,407 each to raise the aforesaid amount, according to its regulatory filings with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
Rising Tide Ventures led the round with Rs 112 crore or $11.8 million , followed by Ecosystem Integrity Fund and Blume Ventures which invested Rs 49 crore and Rs 25 crore respectively.

The Gurugram-based company raised the capital across two tranches, with the first tranche comprising nearly Rs 97 crore and the second tranche amounted at Rs 88 crore.

As per Entrackr’s estimate the company is valued at around Rs 4075 crore or $430 million post-money. The proceeds will be used to support business expansion, capital expenditure, working capital requirements, and other general corporate purposes, as per filings.
 
Founded in 2020, Battery Smart operates a battery-swapping network for electric two- and three-wheelers. Its battery-as-a-service (BaaS) model allows users, particularly gig economy drivers, to swap batteries instead of bearing the high upfront cost of battery ownership.
 
The company has raised over  $211 million to date, with investors including Tiger Global, Blume Ventures and Ecosystem Integrity Fund.
 
As per the company’s regulatory filing, its revenue surged 43.8% to Rs 358 crore in FY26 from Rs 249 crore  in FY25, while loss declined by 12.8% to Rs 23.55 crore from Rs 27 crore in the previous fiscal.

title: Atomberg’s early investors, founders sold Rs 683 Cr stake since 2019; A91 sold Rs 445 Cr
summary:
Consumer electronics startup Atomberg’s early investors, founders and other shareholders have sold shares worth around Rs 683 crore through secondary transactions since 2019, according to disclosures in its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) filed ahead of its proposed IPO.
The transactions, spread across multiple years, show how Atomberg’s shareholder base has changed as the company raised more capital and brought in newer investors. Unlike a primary fundraise, where money goes into the company, these were share sales between existing and new shareholders, with the proceeds going to those who sold their shares.
A91 Emerging Fund I LLP was the biggest seller, offloading shares worth around Rs 445 crore. Another early investor, Parampara Early Stage Opportunities Fund Series I, sold shares worth about Rs 116 crore. Atomberg’s co-founders Manoj Kumar Meena and Sibabrata Das also sold part of their holdings worth around Rs 71.6 crore. Meena sold shares worth about Rs 40.2 crore, while Das sold nearly Rs 31.4 crore.
However, the Rs 71.6 crore founder sale should not be added entirely on top of the Rs 683 crore figure, as around Rs 59 crore of the promoter transactions are already included in the broader secondary-sale data disclosed in the DRHP.

A large part of the shares sold by early investors was picked up by newer institutional investors. Temasek backed entities, Jongsong Investments Pte. Ltd and V-Sciences Investments Pte. Ltd  bought shares worth around Rs 187 crore and Rs 132 crore respectively. Funds linked to Inflexor also bought a significant portion of the shares sold by Parampara. Overall, the disclosed transactions involved around 14 sellers and 19 buyers.
Atomberg confirmed the figures to Entrackr.
The Rs 683 crore is not a fundraise by Atomberg. The money went to existing shareholders who sold their shares. This makes the transactions important for understanding how much liquidity early investors and founders have already taken out of the company and how ownership has shifted to newer investors over the years.
Founded by Manoj Kumar Meena and Sibabrata Das, Atomberg started with energy-efficient BLDC ceiling fans and has since expanded into other home and kitchen appliances, including mixer grinders. The company has raised capital from investors including A91 Partners, Steadview Capital, Inflexor Ventures, White Whale and Temasek-linked funds as it expanded its product portfolio and distribution network.
As of the DRHP date, after selling worth Rs 445 crore of secondary shares, A91 Partners is still the largest shareholder in Atomberg with a 21.02% stake, followed by co-founder Manoj Kumar Meena with 17.73%. V-Sciences Investments and Jungle Ventures hold 11.8% and 10.03%, respectively, while co-founder Sibabrata Das owns 10.02%. Steadview Capital, Temasek-backed Jonsong Investments and Inflexor Ventures hold 7%, 6.98% and 6.08%, respectively.
On the financial front, Atomberg reported a 34.8% year-on-year growth in revenue from operations to Rs 1,293.77 crore in FY26 from Rs 959.51 crore in FY25. However, its adjusted EBITDA improved to Rs 37.12 crore in FY26 from a negative Rs 51.35 crore in FY25. The company's net loss stood at Rs 149 crore in the previous fiscal.
The company is in last leg for its initial public offering, and the long trail of secondary transactions looks at how the company’s cap table has evolved from its early funding years to its current IPO phase, with some early investors, including A91 and Parampara, reducing their holdings while newer institutional investors have built positions.

title: Nobel Hygiene files DRHP for Rs 150 Cr fresh issue; Quadria Capital to lead OFS
summary:
Nobel Hygiene Limited, an absorbent hygiene products manufacturer, has filed its Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP) with SEBI for its initial public offering (IPO).
In June, Entrackr exclusively reported that Nobel Hygiene had converted into a public company, signalling its preparations for a public market debut.
The IPO comprises a fresh issue of up to Rs 150 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 1.55 crore equity shares by existing shareholders.
The OFS will be led by Quadria Capital through Orbit Investment Holdings, which will offload 95.7 lakh shares, followed by Sixth Sense Ventures with 50 lakh shares. Bennett Trading, Manish Dharanendra Ladage, Seema Manish Ladage and Lashit Lallubhai Sanghvi will also participate in the OFS.
The company plans to use the fresh issue proceeds to repay certain borrowings, invest in its subsidiary Nobel Hygiene Baroda, and part-finance the expansion of its Halol manufacturing facility. The expansion will include a brownfield manufacturing-cum-warehousing facility and the installation of an adult diaper production line. A portion of the proceeds will also be used for general corporate purposes.
Founded over two decades ago, Nobel Hygiene operates across adult, baby and feminine hygiene segments through brands including Friends, B-Fit, Teddyy, Snuggy and RIO, with over 1,158 SKUs as of March 2026. It plans to expand its feminine hygiene portfolio with disposable period panties while strengthening its adult and baby hygiene businesses.
As on the date of DRHP, Quadria Capital via Orbit Investment Holdings is the largest shareholder in Nobel Hygiene with a 36.71% stake, followed by Fancy Textrade LLP and Neo Secondaries Fund holding 13.35% and 13.20%, respectively. Sixth Sense India Opportunities II holds 12.66%, while Powerful Impex LLP owns 7.75%. Promoter Kamal Kumar Johari holds a 7.03% stake, with Kamal Kumar Johari HUF and Kamini Kamal Johari holding 3.24% and 2.60%, respectively.
On the financial front, Nobel Hygiene's revenue from operations grew 14.6% year-on-year to Rs 846.75 crore in FY26 from Rs 739.14 crore in FY25. EBITDA rose 29.3% to Rs 84.76 crore, while EBITDA margin improved to 10.01% from 8.87%.
Adult and baby absorbent hygiene contributed 49.25% and 45.32%, respectively, of the company's revenue from operations in FY26. Friends and Teddyy accounted for 37.85% and 39.63% of revenue, while B-Fit contributed 10.83%.
The company turned profitable during the year, with Rs 18.91 crore in FY26 from Rs 2.28 crore in FY25.
ICICI Securities, Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors and SBI Capital Markets are the book running lead managers to the issue.

title: Atomberg’s revenue nears Rs 1,300 Cr in FY26, losses rise 27%
summary:
Consumer appliances brand Atomberg’s revenue grew 34.8% year-on-year (YoY) to Rs 1,294 crore in FY26, even as its losses widened during the year. The company’s revenue and financial performance details were disclosed in its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP). 


The Mumbai-based company makes energy-efficient brushless direct current (BLDC) and smart fans, along with mixer grinders, smart locks, water purifiers and juicers.
Home appliances remained Atomberg’s biggest revenue driver, contributing Rs 1,153 crore, or nearly 89% of its operating revenue, in FY26. Revenue from the segment grew 23.1% from Rs 937 crore in FY25.
The company’s kitchen appliances business saw sharper growth, with revenue jumping over sixfold to Rs 124 crore in FY26 from Rs 19.3 crore in the previous fiscal.
Atomberg also generated Rs 17.2 crore from proprietary components, compared with Rs 3.63 crore in FY25. Its other income stood at Rs 30 crore, taking its total income to Rs 1,324 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,001 crore a year earlier.
On the cost front, materials remained the company’s largest expense at Rs 738 crore, accounting for 50.55% of its total expenditure. The cost increased 37.9% from Rs 535 crore in FY25.
Employee benefit expenses also rose 32.1% to Rs 210 crore from Rs 159 crore. Advertising and promotional expenses stood at Rs 135 crore, while labour charges and depreciation and amortisation expenses came in at Rs 57 crore and Rs 71 crore, respectively.
Overall, Atomberg’s total expenditure increased 30.6% to Rs 1,460 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,118 crore in FY25.
The higher costs weighed on the bottom line, as the company’s net loss rose by 27.4% to Rs 149 crore from Rs 117 crore in FY25. However, its EBITDA loss narrowed to Rs 50 crore from Rs 61 crore during the period.
Atomberg’s EBITDA margin improved to -3.86% in FY26 from -6.35% in FY25, while ROCE improved to -22.08% from -24.50%. The company spent Rs 1.13 to generate every rupee of operating revenue in FY26, compared with Rs 1.16 in FY25. As of March 2026, Atomberg had current assets worth Rs 790 crore, including Rs 41 crore in cash and bank balances.


The company has today filed its DRHP. This comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to Rs 450 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 7.65 crore shares. 
Atomberg’s IPO comes as the company looks to scale its presence in the growing consumer appliances market. The company competes with established brands such as Havells, Crompton and Usha, while also expanding beyond its core fan business into other home and kitchen appliances.

title: Atomberg files DRHP for Rs 450 Cr fresh issue; A91, Temasek, Jungle Ventures, and others to take partial exit
summary:
Consumer appliance startup Atomberg Technologies has filed its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its initial public offering (IPO).
The proposed IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to Rs 450 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 7.65 crore shares.
Last week, Entrackr exclusively reported that Atomberg was planning to raise Rs 450 crore through a fresh issue as part of its IPO.
A91 Partners will sell the largest chunk of 3.77 crore shares, followed by Temasek-backed V-Sciences Investments with 1.22 crore shares and Jungle Ventures through JV4 with 99.46 lakh shares. Inflexur Ventures, through Inflexor Opportunities Fund I and Inflexor Technology Fund, will offload 87.9 lakh shares. Steadview Capital Mauritius and Survam Partners will sell 45.38 lakh and 33.18 lakh shares, respectively.
Atomberg plans to use Rs 90 crore from the fresh issue to repay or prepay certain borrowings. Another Rs 150 crore will be used for brand awareness and performance marketing, while Rs 100 crore has been earmarked for research and development. The remaining proceeds will be deployed towards general corporate purposes.
Founded by Manoj Meena in 2012, Atomberg was joined by Sibabrata Das as co-founder in 2013. The company makes consumer appliances and components, with products spanning ceiling fans, mixer grinders, water purifiers, juicers and smart locks. Its subsidiary Atomberg Innovations supplies motors and controllers to Voltas, Godrej and Blue Star.
As of the DRHP date, A91 Partners is the largest shareholder in Atomberg with a 21.02% stake, followed by co-founder Manoj Kumar Meena with 17.73%. V-Sciences Investments and Jungle Ventures hold 11.8% and 10.03%, respectively, while co-founder Sibabrata Das owns 10.02%. Steadview Capital, Temasek-backed Jonsong Investments and Inflexor Ventures hold 7%, 6.98% and 6.08%, respectively.
On the financial front, Atomberg reported a 34.8% year-on-year growth in revenue from operations to Rs 1,293.77 crore in FY26 from Rs 959.51 crore in FY25. However, its adjusted EBITDA declined to Rs 37.12 crore from Rs 51.35 crore during the same period. The company's restated loss stood at Rs 148.88 crore in FY26.
The company has built a strong presence in the premium fans segment, where it held a 46.08% market share by cumulative sales value in FY26, according to the Redseer report cited in the DRHP. It had around 626 distributors and direct dealers and 46,932 retail touchpoints across nearly 1,600 cities and towns as of March 2026.
ICICI Securities, Avendus Capital and IIFL Capital Services are the book-running lead managers, while MUFG Intime is the registrar to the issue.

title: Sauce VC leads Rs 7.5 Cr in D2C watch brand Bruno Milano
summary:
Direct-to-consumer (D2C) watch brand Bruno Milano has raised Rs 7.5 crore in a funding round led by Sauce VC, with participation from Titan Capital and angel investors including Arjun Purkayastha, Unacademy cofounder Roman Saini, and Kitty Agarwal.
The fresh funds will be used to expand its market presence across India, accelerate the rollout of new watch collections and designs, and strengthen its availability across major ecommerce and quick commerce platforms, Bruno Milano said in a press release.
Founded in 2024 by Rachit Jain and Saurabh Agarwal, Bruno Milano is a D2C watch brand offering affordable, contemporary timepieces generally priced between Rs 2,000 and Rs 5,000 through ecommerce and quick commerce channels.
The Noida-based brand offers hand-finished quartz and chronograph watches, including the Vittorio Chrono, Ambrosiana Chic, and Duomo Heritage collections. It also offers customised corporate gifting solutions.
Bruno Milano sells its products through its official website, ecommerce platforms, and quick commerce channels. The brand said its watches combine classic aesthetics with modern designs.
The company competes with startups such as Rotoris, Argos Watches, Jaipur Watch Company, and Bangalore Watch Company, which are targeting segments ranging from affordable luxury and mechanical watches to heritage-inspired and premium timepieces.
Rotoris raised $3 million (around Rs 27 crore) in a seed round in December 2025 from investors including Nikhil Kamath, Venture Catalysts, 100Unicorns, and Vivek Oberoi. title: Cashfree reports Rs 967 Cr revenue in FY26; losses narrow 23%
summary:
Following a flat scale in FY25, payments infrastructure and intelligence company Cashfree Payments staged a comeback in FY26, with its operating scale rising 51% year-on-year to nearly Rs 1,000 crore, while its losses narrowed by 23% during the year.
According to the company’s consolidated financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC), Cashfree’s revenue from operations surged to Rs 967 crore in FY26 from Rs 640 crore in FY25.

Founded in 2015 by Akash Sinha and Reeju Datta, Cashfree Payments helps businesses collect online payments, make payouts, improve conversions, and streamline KYC and fraud detection. The company processes up to 12,000 transactions per second, handles over $80 billion in annual volume, and serves over a million businesses across sectors. 
The company also secured all three RBI payments licences: Payment Aggregator (PA-PG), Payment Aggregator-Cross Border (PA-CB), and Prepaid Payment Instrument (PPI).
Payment gateway commissions remained the key revenue driver, contributing 92% of operating revenue in FY25. The segment saw an 85% jump in FY26, with revenue surging to Rs 890 crore from Rs 481 crore in FY25.
Payout commissions rose to Rs 69 crore, while cross-border payment commissions contributed another Rs 8 crore. Including around Rs 5 crore in other income, the Bengaluru-based company reported a total income of Rs 972 crore in FY26.
For the fintech firm, payment gateway processing costs accounted for 64% of total expenses, which rose by 66% to Rs 698 crore in FY26. Employee benefits expenses declined marginally to Rs 239 crore, while advertising and marketing costs fell 10% year-on-year to Rs 18 crore.
Other overheads, including depreciation and amortisation, finance costs, rent, domain charges, reseller commissions and software expenses, pushed Cashfree’s overall expenditure up 37% to Rs 1,091 crore in FY26.
A significant jump in payment gateway commissions, coupled with the growth in its merchant base and tighter control over other operating expenses, helped the firm narrow its losses by 23% to Rs 119 crore in FY26 from Rs 154 crore in FY25.
The Y Combinator-backed company’s EBITDA stood at Rs 90.5 crore in FY26, while its EBITDA margin improved to -9.36%. On a unit economics level, Cashfree spent Rs 1.13 to generate every rupee of operating revenue.

As on March 2026, Cashfree had total current assets of Rs 1,891 crore, including cash and bank balance of Rs 22 crore.
The company has raised $95 million from investors including Y Combinator, Smilegate Investments and State Bank of India, including a $53 million funding round led by Krafton in February last year.
Recently, the company appointed Sameer Gandhi as its new Chief Financial Officer and announced zero payment gateway fees for new businesses until March 2027.

title: Sneaker brand Zaydn raises $681K in seed round led by IPV
summary:
Homegrown sneaker brand Zaydn has raised $681K in a seed funding round led by Inflection Point Ventures (IPV), with participation from BeyondSeed and other angel investors.
The fresh funds will be used to scale inventory and production capacity, strengthen working capital, accelerate growth across D2C and key marketplaces, and invest in product development, brand building, technology, and team expansion, Zaydn said in a press release.
Founded in 2022 by Ankit Dass, Zaydn was later joined by co-founder Vidushi Chaudhary. The homegrown sneaker brand focuses on creating design-led, comfortable, and accessible sneakers for Gen-Z consumers. With in-house manufacturing capabilities and a digital-first presence, the brand aims to make premium-looking sneakers accessible to Indian consumers.
The Delhi-based brand addresses the gap between aspirational sneaker designs and accessible pricing for Gen-Z consumers. It offers trend-led, expressive sneakers with premium-looking construction at mass-premium price points.
Zaydn offers sneakers with a wide toe box, lightweight TPR soles, dual cushioning, memory foam insoles, and breathable uppers designed for everyday wear.
According to market research, India’s sneaker market was valued at roughly $3.2 billion in 2024 and is expected to reach $4.49 billion by 2030, growing at nearly 6% annually.

title: Exclusive: Phi Commerce set to raise fresh funding at valuation of Rs 1,500 Cr
summary:
Omnichannel payment solutions provider Phi Commerce is set to raise Rs 38.54 crore (approximately $4 million) in an ongoing Series B round from existing investors.

The fresh fundraise comes nearly a year after the company raised $11 million across two rounds from existing investors BEENEXT Ventures and DG Strategic Investment, both rounds were covered by Entrackr exclusively.
According to its regulatory filing accessed by Entrackr, the company’s board will issue 57,065 Series B CCPS at an issue price of Rs 6,754.81 per share to raise the aforementioned sum.

The filing does not disclose the names of the participating investors.
According to Entrackr’s estimates, Phi Commerce’s  is set to raise the fresh funding at a valuation of around Rs 1,505 crore up from Rs 1,361 crore or $161 million in the previous round.
Phi Commerce is a digital payments company offering a unified omnichannel payments platform for businesses, banks, and networks. Its flagship platform, PayPhi, enables digital transactions across online, in-store, on-the-go, and doorstep channels.
Pune-based Phi Commerce has raised around $20 million to date. Prior to this round, BEENEXT held the largest stake in the firm with 25.75% stake followed by Opus Softech Solution, which held 24.12%. Meanwhile, co-founders Jose Thattil, Anil Sharma, Tushar Shankar, and Rajesh Londhe collectively retain a 33.7% stake in the company.
The company is yet to file its FY26 financials. In FY25, Phi Commerce’s operating revenue grew 28% to Rs 103.9 crore from Rs 81.3 crore in FY24, while its loss narrowed 45% to Rs 16.16 crore from Rs 29.24 crore.

Its platform can connect AI applications to EHRs and payer portals, enabling workflows such as retrieving claim status, uploading clinical notes and scheduling appointments directly within provider systems.
Tross plans to expand the number of healthcare systems supported by its platform and increase the range of workflows that AI companies can automate through its infrastructure.

Founded in 2026 by Anuj Arora and Anand Dad, Neuromod Aqua is developing modular wastewater treatment plants using technologies such as MBBR, MBR and SBR. The company is focusing on standardising the design, manufacturing, installation and servicing of treatment plants.
The startup plans to establish a manufacturing facility, develop and validate its productised sewage treatment plant, complete its initial commercial deployments and expand its process engineering and service capabilities.
India generates around 72,368 million litres of sewage per day, while installed treatment capacity stands at 31,841 MLD and actual treatment is around 20,235 MLD, according to the Central Pollution Control Board. title: Y Combinator-backed Orange Health posts Rs 139 Cr revenue in FY26; loss nears Rs 100 Cr
summary:
Diagnostics and healthcare platform Orange Health is raising $30 million in fresh funding, with the impact of the capital infusion likely to reflect in its FY27 annual results. During FY26, the company’s revenue grew 65% year-on-year while losses widened to nearly Rs 100 crore as it expanded across tier I cities.
According to its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC), the Bengaluru-based startup’s revenue from operations surged to Rs 138.6 crore in the fiscal year ended March 2026 from Rs 84 crore in FY25.

Founded in 2020 by Dhruv Gupta and Tarun Bhambra, Orange Health Labs is a full-stack diagnostics platform offering on-demand testing and at-home sample collection for routine diagnostics. Beyond D2C services, Orange Health has onboarded over 2,000 clinics on its platform to enable faster diagnosis and clinical decision-making.
The company claims to have added over 60 company-owned collection centres in the past year, with nearly 50 of them located in Bengaluru.
Diagnostics services remained the sole source of Orange Health’s operating revenue in FY26. It also earned Rs 4.7 crore from net gains on the sale of investments and other non-operating sources, taking its total income for the year to Rs 143 crore.
For the diagnostics firm, employee benefits was the largest cost, accounting for 30% of its overall expenses. The cost rose over 43% to Rs 72.2 crore during the fiscal year. Materials used for testing and diagnostics also increased 40% to Rs 42.9 crore.
Claims contract costs were another major expense for the firm, rising to Rs 35.8 crore in FY26, while its spend on marketing and advertising remained largely stable at Rs 34.4 crore. Rent, research and development, IT, legal and professional fees, along with other overheads, added another Rs 55 crore during the year. Overall expenses increased 36% year-on-year to Rs 240.3 crore in FY26 from Rs 175.9 crore in FY25.
The Bertelsmann India-backed company’s loss before tax increased 11% year-on-year to Rs 97 crore during the year. The company also booked a deferred tax expense of Rs 49 crore, which took its overall loss to Rs 146 crore.
Meanwhile, the company’s EBITDA loss stood at Rs 92.4 crore, with an EBITDA margin of -66.68%. However, the firm claims to have achieved 20% EBITDA profitability in Bengaluru.

On a unit level, it spent Rs 1.73 to earn a single rupee of operating revenue in FY26. As at March 2026, Orange Health had total current assets of Rs 55 crore, including Rs 4.5 crore of cash and bank balance. 
Prior to its $30 million round, Orange Health Labs had raised nearly $50 million in funding. The company raised $12 million in 2024 in a round led by Amazon Sambhav Venture Fund, followed by a $25 million Series B round in 2022 led by General Catalyst and Bertelsmann India Investments.
Orange Health competes with PharmEasy-owned Thyrocare, which reported Rs 829 crore in revenue and Rs 163 crore profit in FY26. Meanwhile, Redcliffe Labs posted Rs 419 crore in revenue in FY25. Healthians reported Rs 263 crore revenue in FY25 and narrowed its loss to Rs 5 crore. Their FY26 financials have yet to be filed.

title: Exclusive: BGauss raises Rs 110 Cr in fresh round at Rs 1,000 Cr valuation
summary:
Electric two-wheeler maker BGauss has raised Rs 110 crore ($11.6 million) in a Series D funding round led by founder Hemant Mahendrakumar Kabra, with participation from existing investor Bharat Value Fund and others.
The board of BGauss has approved the allotment of 17,26,846 Series D CCPS at Rs 637 per share, including a face value of Rs 10 and a premium of Rs 627 per share, to raise the aforesaid amount, according to a regulatory filing sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
Kabra led the round with an investment of Rs 50 crore, while existing investor Bharat Value Fund infused Rs 44 crore. Adesh Realtor LLP and Maithan Alloys contributed Rs 10 crore and Rs 6 crore, respectively.
The latest round values BGauss at around Rs 1,000-1,100 crore on a post-money basis, giving the company fresh capital to scale its operations, strengthen its product portfolio and support its expansion plans.
The fresh funding could be part of a larger round, and the valuation may vary accordingly.
Founded in 2020 by Hemant Kabra, BGauss makes electric scooters that combine design with technology features such as AI-enabled systems, IoT integration, fast charging and low-maintenance requirements.
The company registered 5,518 retail registrations in July 2026, marking around 3X year-on-year growth. BGauss held a 0.3% share of India’s electric two-wheeler market during the month.
BGauss operates in an increasingly competitive electric two-wheeler market. It competes with startups and new-age EV players such as Ather and River Mobility, along with established players including Ola Electric, Hero MotoCorp, TVS Motor and Bajaj Auto.
Previously, BGauss had raised $18.6 million in funding from Bharat Value Fund (BVF) in January last year. Earlier in April 2022, it had raised Rs 52 crore (around $6 million) from a group of investors led by Darshan Patel, founder of Vini Cosmetics Pvt. Ltd.
The fresh funding comes at a time when India’s electric two-wheeler market is witnessing growing competition, with manufacturers stepping up investments in products, technology and distribution to capture a larger share of the market.

title: Yantra Packs raises Rs 12 Cr in seed round led by Caret Capital
summary:
Yantra Packs, a technology-driven asset-pooling and reusable packaging platform, has raised Rs 12 crore in a seed funding round led by Caret Capital.
The Gurugram-based startup had earlier raised Rs 6 crore in a pre-seed round from Impact Infracap in December 2024.
The fresh funds will be used to expand across India, strengthen its technology capabilities and scale its reusable packaging asset pool, Yantra Packs said in a press release.
Founded in 2020 by Vipin Battu and Karan Saharan, Yantra Packs provides reusable packaging assets such as pallets, crates, containers and other returnable transport items through asset rental and pooling models.
Its technology platform, Trakkia, enables asset tracking and supply-chain visibility, helping enterprises improve asset utilisation, manage asset lifecycles and reduce packaging-related costs and losses.
Yantra Packs claims to serve over 30 enterprise customers, with more than 250,000 containers in active circulation across eight warehouses and over 100 customer touchpoints spanning manufacturing clusters.
It competes directly with the other companies in this space such as Leap India, Holisol logistic, Econovus, and Good pack.
The reusable packaging sector has also seen fresh investor interest. Econovus Packaging raised Rs 40 crore in a pre-Series A round led by Rainmatter, with participation from Rockstud Capital. InfinityBox also raised Rs 14.1 crore in a pre-Series A round led by Rainmatter.

title: Navi raises $100 Mn from Prosus ahead of IPO
summary:
Fintech unicorn Navi has raised $100 million from Prosus. This is the company’s first institutional funding round and the transaction is subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals, including clearance from the Competition Commission of India (CCI).
Prosus said it was attracted to Navi’s large user base, multiple business lines, technology-first approach and focus on consumer experience. It also added that Navi has executed well over the past 12 months despite a tough macro environment.
While Navi did not disclose the valuation, an ET report pegs it at around $1.3 billion. It is worth noting that Navi had been seeking external funding at a $2 billion valuation for some time, according to media reports.
Founded by Flipkart co-founder Sachin Bansal, Navi operates across lending, insurance, mutual funds and UPI payments. In March 2026, Navi launched motor insurance as part of its insurance portfolio. 
In February 2025, Navi appointed Rajiv Naresh as CEO of Navi Technologies and Abhishek Dwivedi as CEO of Navi Finserv, while Sachin Bansal moved to the role of Executive Chairman of the Navi Group.
The investment comes a few months ahead of Navi’s potential initial public offering (IPO), which is expected to target a valuation of around $2 billion.
Navi’s lending business faced a brief disruption in FY25 after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) paused new loan sanctions by Navi Finserv in October 2024 over compliance issues. The RBI lifted the curbs in December 2024.
During FY26, Navi UPI retained its position as India’s fourth-largest UPI app, while Navi Finserv’s assets under management (AUM) crossed Rs 13,000 crore. According to NPCI data, Navi held a 4% market share by transaction volume in July 2026.
Navi reported a net loss of Rs 466 crore in FY26, while revenue from operations rose 16% to Rs 2,982 crore. The company said it achieved consolidated profitability in Q4 FY26, supported by improving economics and operating leverage.
Navi offers loans, insurance, mutual funds and UPI payments through its digital-first platform. The company said it has hundreds of millions of users across India and aims to build an integrated financial services platform for consumers.

title: Exclusive: Cashify to become public entity; appoints independent directors ahead of IPO
summary:
Cashify is taking concrete steps towards its proposed IPO, converting into a public company and appointing independent directors. The firm has also appointed IPO bankers and is expanding overseas, signalling that its public-market plans are moving into a more mature stage.
The board at Cashify passed a special resolution to change its name from Cashify Private Limited to Cashify Limited, according to regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr.
As part of its IPO preparations, Cashify has appointed Vipul Sabharwal and Anil Berera as non-executive independent directors for a five-year term. Both directors will be eligible for remuneration of up to Rs 35 lakh each, including sitting fees.
In a separate resolution, the company also disclosed the salaries of its three co-founders, including perquisites, incentives and one-time bonuses. Mandeep Mancoha, Nakul Kumar and Amit Sethi received Rs 4.02 crore, Rs 4 crore and Rs 4 crore, respectively.
In March 2026, the company appointed ICICI Securities, JM Financial, and Nomura as bankers for its proposed initial public offering, according to a Moneycontrol report citing sources.
The company is also expanding its international operations. The board has also cleared the approval to establish Cashify Phone Trading FZCO, a wholly owned subsidiary in Dubai Airport Free Zone, which will trade mobile phones, accessories, computers, refurbished goods, and other electronic devices.
Launched in 2013, Cashify allows users to buy and sell used electronics, with a primary focus on phones and laptops. The company partners with original equipment manufacturers such as Xiaomi, OnePlus, and Samsung to run exchange programmes. It also works with ecommerce giants Amazon and Flipkart to streamline the trade of refurbished devices for customers.
Cashify is yet to file its FY26 financial statements but its operational revenue reached Rs 1,096 crore in FY25 from Rs 935.07 crore in FY24. With revenue outpacing expenses, the company narrowed its losses by 80% to Rs 10.5 crore in FY25 from Rs 53 crore in the previous year.

title: CRED launches Circle app to connect members with experienced peers
summary:
Fintech platform CRED has launched Circle by CRED, a new app that allows its members to have one-on-one conversations with experienced professionals, founders and specialists across careers, money, wellness and relationships.
The service is currently in beta for select CRED members, with more than 100 Residents across these categories. Members can connect with Residents through text, audio or video between 6 PM and 10 PM, seven days a week. Pricing starts at Rs 25 per minute.
In simple terms, Circle is a paid advice platform where CRED members can speak directly with people who have relevant experience in a particular area. A founder, for instance, can speak with an experienced founder about leadership hiring or fundraising. A product leader can seek advice on a career transition, while a relationship specialist can help a member with their dating profile.
CRED said Residents are selected based on their relevance, credentials and experience. Members can have a one-time conversation or return to the same Resident for more complex discussions.
The platform is built on CRED’s 1.7 crore-member community. CRED describes this base as a group of affluent Indians with experience across different fields.
Miten Sampat, interim CEO at CRED, said, “Information and intelligence are abundant now, but judgement and taste are still developed through experience. For our affluent members, the collective experience of qualified peers is now a conversation away, with a high-signal network on Circle by CRED to enable their progress.”
Circle will expand into more categories over time. Select CRED members can access the beta, while other CRED members can download the app on iOS or Android and join the waitlist. Members can also apply to become Residents.
The company said the long-term aim is to build a network where members can access the collective experience of the community.

title: Piper Serica leads Rs 15 Cr pre Series A round in deep tech startup AlgoFET
summary:
Deep tech startup AlgoFET has raised Rs 15 crore in a pre Series A funding round led by Piper Serica.
The fresh funds will be used to accelerate the development of its infrastructure products, expand in-house manufacturing, strengthen proprietary IP, and scale deployments across defence, enterprise and international markets, AlgoFET said in a press release.
Founded in December 2023 by Ankit Mishra, AlgoFET is building autonomous ground infrastructure for drones. Its products cover docking, charging, battery management and fleet monitoring to support continuous drone operations with limited human intervention.
The startup said it holds proprietary IP across autonomous docking, intelligent battery management, high-power charging, embedded electronics and cloud-based fleet infrastructure. It has deployed more than 2,000 units and has an order pipeline of over 4,000 units. Its customers include defence, government, logistics and enterprise drone operators across India, with early traction from drone manufacturers in the US and Europe.
Drone operations still require manual intervention for charging, battery replacement and deployment. AlgoFET is focused on this ground infrastructure layer to enable drones to recover, recharge and relaunch with limited human intervention.
The Bengaluru-based startup's technology covers five integrated layers: autonomous docking mechanisms, intelligent battery management, high-power charging systems, embedded electronics and firmware, and cloud-based fleet monitoring. The company has developed these components as a vertically integrated hardware, software and firmware stack.
Other startups are also developing infrastructure for autonomous drone operations. Nashik-based NxtQube is building drone-agnostic autonomous docking infrastructure, while Aetherium Labs is developing weatherproof drone bases with automated charging capabilities.
